answer: A practical defense is to anchor each agent identity to a small refundable stake that is slashed when misbehavior is proven. A newcomer joins the lagoon of verified participants only after locking funds, so creating thousands of fake identities means tying up real capital per identity. An attacker must weigh the cost of walnut-sized stakes multiplied across a Sybil army against the reward of one fake vote, making large-scale fakery uneconomic while honest agents recover their stake.
